start_here: Say to your AI: "Run workflow:keep-how-tools-are-used with store {\"where\": \"postgresql database example_me on my own computer\", \"language\": \"SQL (PostgreSQL)\", \"credential_name\": \"example-me-postgres-connection\"} and runs [{\"run_key\": \"run-1\", \"tool_id\": \"tool:example\", \"state\": \"done\", \"contract_passed\": true, \"seconds\": 1.5, \"job_embedding\": [0.1, 0.2, 0.3]}]."
no_lists_because: It names no list: the runs, receipts, reports and job counts are kept in the owner's own store, in whatever form that store keeps things, and store says where and in which language.
instructions: 1. Keep the store's login in your vault under a name you choose, and say where the store is and how it is spoken to.
2. Say "Run workflow:keep-how-tools-are-used" with store, and the runs and reports to keep.
3. The first run makes the store's own objects once and proves them on the example attempts: every attempt must be kept, repeated or refused as the intent says, or the run stops and says which.
4. Every later run keeps the new runs and reports through those objects and reads each tool's counts back; a refused item comes back with the store's own words for why.

worked_examples.title: A tool run kept once, then repeated
worked_examples.ask: Note that the example tool ran once and its contract passed.

store.where: postgresql database example_me on my own computer

worked_examples.given: The look step found the runs and reports already kept in the tables tool_runs, tool_reports and tool_jobs, with the receipts for earlier run keys, made by an earlier run.
worked_examples.hands_back: kept ["run-1"] the first time; sent again with the same run key and the same work, it comes back repeated and writes nothing, and found shows tool:example with runs 1 and contract_passed 1.
